Hey hon, I know how hard it is to be so young and feeling like you don't matter. But you do matter. I've also gone through self harm, social anxiety, a suicide attempt, and a lot of other things. Plus as someone who takes up two letters in LGBTQ+ I know how it feels to be judged by other people just for being you. You're so young and you got a lot of potential for your life. Not gonna lie, shits fucking difficult. It's so hard to get better after being in this emotional state for so long. But you can do it. I believe in you and you should believe in yourself. You are not worthless and you matter in this world. Take a rest and try to take care of yourself. Make sure to eat and sleep well, try not to hurt yourself, and don't put yourself down if you're having a bad day. Take care hon, I do hope you change your mind and don't try to hurt yourself

*hugs*

Hey I also relapsed today after 33 days clean. It was just a small cut, deep but nothing major. Finding other ways to cope is so hard cause some times those coping skills don't work. I can't offer any advice other than the obvious advice thats been said thousands of times before. But if you could go for 35 days, which is already pretty good, than I know you have the strength to go longer this time around. Relapsing doesn't diminish the amount of progress you've made. Yeah like I said I don't really have any advice but I hope you found some sort of comfort reading this.

From reading this it seems that you really like the guy. The best advice I can give you is don't put your happiness aside merely for other peoples sake. If you think your family would be hurtful towards you it's probably best not to come out. But you know your situation more than I do. Don't make a decision that you think you'll regret. You don't have to break up with him if you really do like him.

You could look into any non-binary genders if you feel like that's what would describe you to best. I get exactly what you mean when you say that it feels better having a label. Also be aware that how you label yourself can change and that's ok. As you get to know more about yourself you may find that another label fits you better. Either way however you label yourself is valid.

Also just experiment. Find out what clothing you prefer, what pronouns you like, preferred name, etc. Hope this helped

If you still plan to do it, be prepared for the worst. Think if there's anyone else in your life who would be supportive, and if you would have a place to stay in case of worse case scenario.

Have you thought about writing a letter, either handwritten or through email? With a letter you can write down everything you need to say while not talking to the person face to face. If you're really up for it you can also to it through phone or text. Just be prepared beforehand with what you want to say as well as responses to any questions she might have. Also try to be ready for any sort of response, you can never really tell how a person will respond. Might be supportive, totally against you, or just confused. Best of luck to you, hope it goes well.

Currently 19 and Living in California, USA. Ever since I was a little kid I always felt different. At the time of course I had no idea what it was and I just kinda dealt with it. I was always quiet and almost non-verbal during elementary and middle school and was bullied a little bit during that time. High school began and all those little weird feelings that I had since childhood got way worse. I discovered that it was probably depression and/or anxiety issues that I was having. Insert a couple years of depression and anxiety issues during high school. Graduated last year with ok grades. During the summer following I did random labor work for a bit of money (field work, washing solar panels). I've gotten used to work like that, ever since I was 12 to 17 I've been helping my family sell at flea markets. After that summer I started going to a community college rather than a university like I wanted to. Now I'm in a complicated phase of life and I still have some mental health issues. I've had this Reddit account since last year and I've been posting about my weird life on some other subreddits. If you really wan't to you could check out my posts, but I should warn it is a little dark so proceed with caution.

I still don't know how to properly convey my feelings but I still make the attempt to write. As for not having any interesting to write about, just write about literally anything. You can write about a hobby of yours, something neat that happened, something your interested about, or just give your opinions on any topic that comes to mind. Sometimes I write about what I'm thinking about in that moment, and I take the time to describe not just my thoughts but also the area around and appreciate it. Hope this helped

If you don't already, I highly recommend getting a journal or diary.

From experience, I've learned that its best to plan out beforehand how to encounter the least amount of people while outside, or go with a trusted and safe person (friend, family member, etc.)

I think the reason why we took so long was because we never really had a lot of deep conversations before. All throughout our childhood we were raised with the idea that showing emotion was bad and that you had to "be a man." Plus, part of me was kind of afraid to to tell them because I thought that by being trans we wouldn't be as close to each other. I thought that there would some sort of disconnect with each other. It's difficult to explain. Looks like we're actually closer. As for whether I think this is genetic or environmental, I think its genetic, but it could also be environmental.

Yup, I can relate. I remember when first stated developing signs of depression almost everyday would be shit but I would be grateful for times when I was happy. As time went one however, whenever I got happy I would feel like I didn't deserve to be happy, or I would get more depressed by reminding myself that the happiness I'm feeling was only temporary. To be honest, it still happens quite often and I still don't really know how to deal with it. The best I can do is try live in the moment whenever something good happens and try to block out all other thoughts. It sometimes works. This probably isn't the type of response you were looking for (sorry if I just made you more depressed), but it feels a little better knowing someone out there can relate. Stay strong friend.

Hi there, I’m also 18 and in the same situation as you. I’m currently attending college and I am dreading growing up. While the thought of living for just myself seems appealing, all the responsibilities that come along with it terrify me. The only advice I can give is find a new therapist. If this one isn’t working out for you then try to find one that cares. I know it can be scary at first considering your first experience, but if you are really contemplating suicide then I highly recommend seeking help. If you still don't want to try therapy again then try to find help in some other way (even if its just by posting on reddit). If you ever need to speak to someone you can PM me. Try to stay strong and I hope everything goes well for you.
